extracted.intended_audience: businesses/marketers, consumer protection counsel, and consumers following FTC enforcement
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of FTC enforcement standards and factual examples addressing deceptive or misleading commercial conduct (subscription practices, MLM earnings claims, impersonation, fake reviews, deceptive pricing, etc.). The page lists cases, press releases, and actions illustrating what the FTC treats as unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 5 (FTC Act) violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violations of Section 5 of the FTC Act (unfair or deceptive acts or practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly frames enforcement as Section 5 allegations (e.g., Uber charged consumers without consent and made false claims). Examples include charging without consent, failing to deliver promised benefits, and making false or misleading statements about products or services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore Online Shoppers’ Confidence Act (ROSCA) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements under ROSCA for online negative option features and recurring charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC alleges companies using negative options must obtain consumer consent and comply with ROSCA. Example: the Uber complaint alleges charges for Uber One via a negative option feature and ROSCA violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative-option feature cancellation mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers using negative-option (subscription/recurring) billing must provide a simple mechanism to stop recurring charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Uber complaint alleges Uber 'failed to provide a simple mechanism to stop recurring charges.' This implies a requirement for an easy, consumer-facing cancellation process when subscriptions auto-renew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer consent for charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Businesses must not charge consumers for services or subscriptions without the consumer's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites allegations that companies 'charged consumers without their consent' (Uber). Ensuring clear, verifiable consent is required for recurring or subscription charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of cancellation claims ('cancel anytime')
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that consumers can 'cancel anytime' must be truthful and not contradicted by fees or obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC alleges Uber 'falsely claims that consumers can cancel Uber One at “any time” with no additional fees.' Marketing claiming 'cancel anytime' must reflect actual cancellation terms and not mislead about fees or obstacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful savings and benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Representations about savings or benefits (e.g., subscription savings) must be accurate and substantiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC alleged Uber 'failed to deliver promised savings.' Marketers must not promise savings or benefits they cannot substantiate or routinely fail to deliver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on deceptive earnings claims (MLMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: MLM participants and operators must not use false or baseless claims about how much money workers/participants can earn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple entries note FTC action against MLM participants for 'deceiving consumers about the amount of money they could earn' and 'deceptive earnings claims.' Typical guidance: earnings claims must be truthful, not misleading as to typical results, and supported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No impersonation of government or trusted entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities must not impersonate the government or large carriers/organizations to induce purchases or enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a nationwide operation was temporarily halted for allegedly 'impersonat[ing] the government and large insurance carriers to deceive consumers seeking health insurance.' Misrepresenting affiliation with government or major institutions is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful affiliation and coverage claims in health/insurance offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Health insurance and related offerings must not misrepresent coverage, comprehensiveness, or affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC sought a halt to an operation that allegedly sold 'supposedly comprehensive PPO plans that do not offer the coverage they seek.' Representations about coverage scope and affiliations must be accurate and not misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on deceptive product effectiveness claims and testimonial manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about a product's effectiveness must be substantiated; using reviews written by employees or incentivized reviews without disclosure is deceptive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from TruHeight: defendants 'deceptively advertised the effectiveness of a range of supplements... and relied on reviews that were written by their own employees, or by consumers who were offered a free product or discount in return for writing a 5-star review.' Testimonials and reviews must reflect genuine, disclosed experiences and material connections must be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fraudulent or dishonest timeshare-exit schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators may not take consumers' money to 'exit' timeshares and then fail to provide the promised services or defraud consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A court ordered an operator of a timeshare exit scheme to pay $140 million related to allegations the scheme 'took millions from consumers.' Sellers of services must actually provide the services and not use fraudulent promises to obtain funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent pricing; prohibition on junk fees and unwanted add-ons
rubrics_metrics.description: Businesses must not systemically deceive customers with hidden fees, unwanted add-on products, or overcharges at point of sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC and state action against Lindsay Automotive Group resulted in refunds for 'deceptive pricing practices and unwanted add-ons.' Pricing must be transparent and add-ons must be clearly disclosed and optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of vulnerable or targeted populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Schemes that specifically target vulnerable groups (e.g., older adults) are subject to enforcement and heightened scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Square One Development Group case alleges scamming 'mostly older adults' out of more than $90 million. Targeting vulnerable consumers can be an aggravating enforcement factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of law enforcement and court remedies (TROs, halting operations, settlements, bans, refunds)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the FTC alleges deception or imminent consumer harm, courts may issue temporary restraining orders, halt nationwide operations, require refunds, impose penalties, and permanently prohibit deceptive practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page examples: courts temporarily halted operations (Florida health-insurance impersonation), ordered $140M recovery in timeshare case, and permanently prohibited MLM operators from deceptive earnings claims; FTC actions may seek full refunds and additional penalties to redress consumers.
